true_statement: Are the Fine-tuned-prt bars consistently closer to zero than the MistralV0.2-Base bars across all specialties? Is this correct?
false_statement: Are the MistralV0.2-Base bars consistently closer to zero than the Fine-tuned-prt bars across all specialties? Is this correct?
fact_description: The Fine-tuned-prt bars are consistently shorter (less negative) than the MistralV0.2-Base bars
true_response: Yes, the Fine-tuned-prt bars (all colored bars) are consistently closer to zero (i.e., less negative) than the MistralV0.2-Base bars (light blue) across all specialties. This is correct and indicates that fine-tuning improves performance (lower negative log probability = better likelihood) in all cases shown.
false_response: No, the MistralV0.2-Base bars are not consistently closer to zero than the Fine-tuned-prt bars across all specialties. In fact, in five of the six specialties (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), the fine-tuned models (especially those fine-tuned on the same specialty) achieve less negative (better) log probabilities than the base model. Only in the Neuro specialty does the base model outperform all fine-tuned variants. Therefore, the statement is incorrect.

evaluation.reasoning: The model agrees with the true statement and disagrees with the false statement, demonstrating consistent and correct understanding of the visual evidence.
